interactions.label: Obstruction of the uveoscleral pathway alone would be sufficient to explain the

params.question: Obstruction of the uveoscleral pathway alone would be sufficient to explain the raised intraocular pressure seen in most forms of glaucoma.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: The uveoscleral pathway handles only 10–15 per cent of aqueous drainage. The conventional pathway — trabecular meshwork → Schlemm's canal → episcleral veins — carries 85–90 per cent. Since this major route is where most glaucomas obstruct drainage, blocking the minor uveoscleral route alone cannot explain the degree of pressure rise seen in glaucoma.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Well reasoned. The uveoscleral route handles only 10–15 per cent of aqueous outflow. Most forms of glaucoma involve obstruction of the conventional pathway — through the trabecular meshwork, Schlemm's canal, and the episcleral veins — which carries 85–90 per cent of total drainage. Blocking the minor route alone cannot produce the significant pressure elevations seen clinically.

interactions.label: A 65-year-old patient has no symptoms but shows progressive optic disc cupping.

params.question: A 65-year-old patient has no symptoms but shows progressive optic disc cupping. Gonioscopy reveals a wide-open iridocorneal angle with no visible deposits or structural abnormalities. Based on the four-mechanism framework, which pathological process explains this silent pressure rise?

answers.text: Arrested neural crest cell migration preventing angle maturation from birth

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes trabeculodysgenesis in congenital glaucoma, which presents in infancy with buphthalmos and corneal changes — not in a 65-year-old with a structurally normal angle.

answers.text: Gradual accumulation of extracellular matrix in the juxtacanalicular tissue with progressive loss of trabecular endothelial cells

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In primary open-angle glaucoma, extracellular matrix builds up in the juxtacanalicular tissue adjacent to Schlemm's canal over decades. Trabecular endothelial cells are gradually lost. The angle appears normal on gonioscopy, yet outflow resistance rises silently — which is precisely what makes this condition so dangerous.

answers.text: Pupil block from lens-iris apposition causing the iris to bow forward and seal the angle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pupil block is the mechanism of primary angle-closure glaucoma, which presents acutely with a closed angle — the opposite of this patient's wide-open angle on gonioscopy.

answers.text: Deposition of pseudoexfoliation material clogging the trabecular meshwork

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pseudoexfoliation material is an identifiable secondary cause visible on slit-lamp examination as white fibrillar deposits on the anterior lens capsule. The question specifies no visible deposits or structural abnormalities.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key clue is the open, apparently normal angle with no visible cause. Primary open-angle glaucoma involves microscopic changes — extracellular matrix accumulation and endothelial cell loss in the juxtacanalicular tissue — that are invisible on gonioscopy but silently increase outflow resistance over decades.

Correct. The open, apparently normal angle is precisely what makes primary open-angle glaucoma so dangerous — the pathology is microscopic, at the level of the juxtacanalicular tissue, and invisible on gonioscopy.

interactions.label: A 55-year-old woman presents with acute eye pain, nausea, coloured haloes, and a

params.question: A 55-year-old woman presents with acute eye pain, nausea, coloured haloes, and a mid-dilated fixed pupil after watching a film in a darkened cinema. Which pathophysiological sequence best explains her presentation?

answers.text: Prolonged near work caused ciliary muscle spasm, raising intraocular pressure in an open angle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ciliary muscle spasm from near work causes accommodation and pupil constriction, which actually pulls the peripheral iris away from the angle — the opposite of what triggers an acute attack.

answers.text: Dim light dilated the pupil, maximising lens-iris apposition and trapping aqueous behind the iris, which bowed forward to seal the trabecular meshwork

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: In a predisposed narrow-angle eye, dim light produces mid-dilation of the pupil, maximising the area of lens-iris contact (pupil block). Trapped aqueous pushes the iris forward (iris bombé), sealing the trabecular meshwork and causing an acute pressure spike — the classic cinema sign.

answers.text: Light adaptation caused pupil constriction, compressing the trabecular meshwork against Schlemm's canal

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pupil constriction pulls the peripheral iris away from the trabecular meshwork, opening the angle. This is why pilocarpine — a miotic that constricts the pupil — is used to treat acute angle-closure, not cause it.

answers.text: Emotional stress triggered hypersecretion of aqueous humour by the ciliary body, overwhelming outflow capacity

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Aqueous hypersecretion is not the mechanism of angle-closure glaucoma. The problem is obstructed outflow caused by mechanical iris apposition against the trabecular meshwork, not overproduction of fluid.

overallFeedback.feedback: In a narrow-angle eye, dim light dilates the pupil to a mid position, maximising lens-iris contact. Aqueous trapped behind the iris pushes it forward (iris bombé), physically sealing the trabecular meshwork — causing the dramatic emergency presentation of acute angle-closure glaucoma.
Correct. The cinema sign is a classic trigger — dim light mid-dilates the pupil in a predisposed narrow-angle eye, maximising pupil block and causing acute angle-closure.

interactions.label: A young myopic male presents with acute blurred vision and raised intraocular pr

params.question: A young myopic male presents with acute blurred vision and raised intraocular pressure after vigorous exercise. Slit-lamp examination reveals a vertical band of brown pigment on the corneal endothelium. Which secondary glaucoma does this presentation indicate?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Pseudoexfoliation glaucoma produces white fibrillar deposits on the anterior lens capsule, not pigmented corneal deposits. It is the commonest secondary open-angle glaucoma worldwide but typically affects older patients.

In pigmentary glaucoma, a concave iris rubs against the lens zonules and sheds melanin granules that deposit on the corneal endothelium as a Krukenberg spindle — the vertical brown band seen here. The classic patient is a young myopic male, and exercise dislodges additional pigment, causing acute pressure spikes.
Phacolytic glaucoma occurs when leaked proteins from a hypermature cataract clog the trabecular meshwork. It is unrelated to exercise-triggered pressure spikes or corneal pigment deposits.
Steroid-induced glaucoma requires a history of corticosteroid use and resolves when the steroid is discontinued. It does not produce pigmented deposits on the corneal endothelium.

overallFeedback.feedback: The vertical pigment band on the corneal endothelium (Krukenberg spindle), a young myopic male patient, and exercise-triggered pressure spikes together form the classic triad of pigmentary glaucoma — caused by a concave iris rubbing against the lens and shedding melanin granules.

Correct. The Krukenberg spindle — a vertical band of melanin granules on the corneal endothelium — combined with a young myopic male and exercise-triggered pressure spike is the classic triad of pigmentary glaucoma.

interactions.label: A newly diagnosed open-angle glaucoma patient tells you their vision seems perfe

params.question: A newly diagnosed open-angle glaucoma patient tells you their vision seems perfectly fine and asks why they should use drops every night. Based on the counselling approach described, which is the most effective opening response?

answers.text: Your eye pressure is dangerously high and you may go blind within months if untreated

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Alarmist language generates anxiety without building understanding. Effective counselling uses clear, factual statements that explain what the treatment does and does not do.

answers.text: These drops do not make your vision better — they prevent further loss of the vision you still have

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This statement directly addresses the commonest cause of early discontinuation — the expectation that drops should produce noticeable improvement. Reframing the goal as preservation rather than restoration helps the patient understand that the absence of change is itself the treatment success, much like blood pressure medication.

answers.text: Most patients who stop their drops do not notice any change for several years

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While slow progression may be factually true in early disease, this response inadvertently reinforces the belief that stopping drops has no consequences — undermining the very adherence you are trying to build.

answers.text: The drops will gradually restore the peripheral vision you have already lost

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Glaucomatous optic nerve damage is irreversible. Drops prevent further loss but cannot restore vision already lost. Promising restoration sets false expectations that lead to disappointment and discontinuation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The video emphasised that the key counselling message is: 'These drops do not make your vision better — they prevent further loss.' Addressing this misconception at the first visit prevents the commonest cause of early treatment discontinuation.

Correct. The single most important message at the first visit is that drops protect remaining vision — they do not restore lost vision. This prevents the commonest reason patients stop their glaucoma treatment.
